_: Round 420 (language C). The five pins round 416 measured `shadowed`, each re-pointed to a guardian SIGHTED in its own direction. `guardian_was` is the label round 416 named; `repoint_why` is why the new one is the right one. Candidates came from `python3 polarity.py repoint`; the pick among them is by MECHANISM and is the author's.

pins.mechanism: M3 miss_names_unbound: the clause fires only for an UNBOUND name
pins.guardian: guest miss <unbound name> names the miss-reason cure
pins.predicate: contains(A, s) and not contains(A, t)
pins.why: the clause never fires at all. The guardian's positive half reads the ordinary unbound-name text, which survives; its negative half is satisfied a fortiori.
pins.guardian_was: guest miss <BOUND name> stays plain propagation
pins.repoint_why: M3 is a biconditional -- the cure clause fires for an UNBOUND name and for no other. Round 416 pointed the `-` edit (the clause never fires at all) at the BOUND-name half, which is the half that agrees with the mutant: a bound name gets no clause either way. The UNBOUND half is the one the edit moves, it is `contains(...)` and therefore SIGHTED on `-`, and it went red in round 416's own campaign.

pins.mechanism: M5 eval_if: a non-boolean condition is a miss (decision: no truthiness)
pins.why: EVERY condition is refused -- the evaluator misses more. A `missed(...)` guardian is monotone in exactly this direction.
pins.repoint_why: M5's `+` edit refuses EVERY condition. `missed(gv("if 1 {...}"))` is monotone along refusal and cannot see that; the check that an ordinary `if true` still evaluates is two-sided and dies immediately. The pair `guest if` / `guest strict if rejects 0` already spans both directions -- round 416 named the wrong one of the two.

pins.mechanism: M8 is_num excludes a Guess (Guess arithmetic is transparent)
pins.guardian: guest return type accepts a matching value
pins.why: is_num rejects EVERYTHING. A `not is_num(...)` guardian is monotone in this direction by construction.
pins.guardian_was: is_num rejects a guess wrapping a number
pins.repoint_why: M8's `+` edit makes `is_num` answer false for everything. `not is_num(guess(...))` is monotone along rejection. The `-> num` return contract ACCEPTING 5 is the positive use of `is_num` in the same file, is two-sided, and is the direction the negative check cannot see.

pins.mechanism: M10 apply_binop delegates `==` to the host when either side is a Guess
pins.why: ALWAYS delegate: guest_eq is bypassed for every ==, so the guest-authored opaque-closure comparator never runs
pins.needle: if is_guess_val(a.v) or is_guess_val(b.v) { a.v == b.v }
pins.guardian_was: top-level == between two guesses yields a new guess
pins.repoint_why: M10's `+` edit delegates EVERY `==` to the host. The named guardian's probe is two guesses, which delegate under both rules -- probe agreement, not predicate blindness (`is_guess(...)` is `-`-blind, not `+`-blind). The NESTED comparison is the case the two rules disagree on, and it is the only sighted co-red candidate.

pins.mechanism: M12 check_ret is a no-op over an already-missed body (decision 2)
pins.guardian: guest return type rejects a mismatched value
pins.why: the return contract is removed entirely. 1/0 still misses, so the guardian is still green.
pins.guardian_was: guest return type is not re-checked over an already-missed body
pins.repoint_why: M12's `-` edit deletes the return contract outright. The named guardian asserts what the contract does NOT do to an already-missed body, and deleting the contract satisfies that a fortiori. That a mismatched value still misses is the claim the deletion breaks.
